headline: Stress-testing single-cell inference: when causal and correlational GRN methods fail
label: Single Cell Transcriptomic Inference Methods
summary: Benchmarks and controlled diagnostics now test where single-cell inference methods fail, alongside sample- and spatially constrained cell-level assignment.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of cell-level and sample-level biology from single-cell and spatial transcriptomes, with growing emphasis on defining the conditions under which inference breaks. The GRN study isolates seven pathologies, including dropout, confounders and feedback, to test when causal versus correlational methods hold. SCMBench benchmarks 23 domain-specific and foundation models for single-cell multi-omics integration across accuracy, biomarkers, trajectories and batch correction. DEGAS transfers patient-level disease attributes to individual spatial transcriptomic cells with spatial smoothing, while MUSTARD and PyFgsea add sample-aware and trajectory-aware analysis. What is new is controlled stress-testing of inference under known pathologies, combined with spatially and sample-constrained cell-level assignment. geneSync and nested-WGCNA address harmonization and bulk co-expression tasks outside this single-cell focus.
